newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Indian Maruti car exports go through Colombo port.
newsitem.headline: Indian Maruti car exports go through Colombo port.

text.p: Colombo port on Friday began transshipping more than 3,000 Maruti cars made by Suzuki Motor Corp in India, port officials said.
"This is the first time direct transshipment of vehicles is taking place in Colombo," an official at the Jaye Container Terminal said.
The cars arrived from Navasheva, on India's west coast, and were bound for the Netherlands, Greece and Italy, he said.
Colombo port, south Asia's transshipment hub, would earn a $25 charge per vehicle, he said.
Other foreign manufacturers making cars in India had inquired about transshipping car exports through Colombo, port officials said.
The officials said several vessels bound for Bombay had diverted to Colombo to discharge cargo because of the strike by truckers in India.
"We have a bunch of ships outside the port. They can't go to to Bombay," an official said.
An estimated 2.2 million trucks pulled their vehicles off the roads across India on Tuesday.

The owners demand the withdrawal of the government's five percent service tax on road transport proposed in the 1997/98 federal budget and the scrapping of a decision by state-owned insurance firms to boost insurance premiums sharply.
